claims.text: The initial material is cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance.
The proposed intervention is preoxidation at 950–1000 °C and 10⁻⁵–10⁻⁴ atm oxygen partial pressure for 1–2 hours.
The specified preoxidation treatment will form a thin, dense surface oxide scale.
The preoxidation scale will be composed primarily of Hf, Zr, and Ti oxides.
The preoxidation scale will be adherent and passivating.
A protective surface layer can impede high-temperature oxidation of a refractory high-entropy alloy.
The proposed Hf–Zr–Ti oxide scale will minimize oxygen diffusion into the HfNbTaTiZr bulk.
The underlying HfNbTaTiZr alloy has a BCC microstructure.
The underlying BCC microstructure governs the alloy's mechanical performance.
The preoxidation treatment will not affect the underlying BCC microstructure.
After 100 hours at 1000 °C in air, preoxidized specimens will have significantly lower oxygen uptake than untreated specimens.
After 100 hours at 1000 °C in air, preoxidized specimens will exhibit less oxide-scale spallation than untreated specimens.
The preoxidized alloy will retain its original yield strength after high-temperature exposure.
The preoxidized alloy will retain its original tensile ductility after high-temperature exposure.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr undergoes rapid oxygen ingress and oxidation-induced mechanical degradation at high temperature.
Departures from the proposed processing and service conditions may change scale protectiveness or mechanical performance.

contradictions.description: The mechanical boundary is expressed as strain-rate-controlled loading, whereas the experiment specifies a constant mechanical load 'corresponding to' a strain rate. Constant-load and strain-rate-controlled tests are distinct loading modes, so the proposed loading condition is internally inconsistent.
